name: Chariot
evidence: Headline: Exclusive: Chariot Raises $10M To Help Consumers Fight Back Against Hidden Fees And Hard-To-Cancel Subscriptions

Summary: New York-based Chariot Claims has raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Silverton Partners to help consumers pursue claims over alleged privacy violations, hidden fees and subscriptions that are difficult to cancel.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Chariot Claims is a Brooklyn/NYC legal-tech platform that helps consumers identify and file claims (privacy violations, hidden fees, hard-to-cancel subscriptions) against companies, working with a network of law firms and building AI tools to screen and process claims.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: CEO (Zim Hang) has a non-technical background (psychology/neuroscience degree; prior fintech/healthtech/web3 ventures), so founder technical depth rests mainly on the CTO rather than both co-founders.

Core business model (mass consumer claims/arbitration against companies, paired with a law firm network) looks more like a claims-processing/legal-ops operation than a defensible AI or infrastructure product; the AI layer ('developing AI tools to review documents') appears early/in-progress rather than a shipped core differentiator.
Mass arbitration business models face periodic regulatory and reputational scrutiny, which is a business-risk factor for an early employee to weigh.
assessment.rationale: This is a real, revenue-generating consumer-facing legal-tech company (200k+ monthly submissions, ~15 people, breaking even) in a vertical the person weights highly (applied AI in legal), based in NYC which matches their geographic preference, raising a reasonably sized Series A ($10M) within their preferred range. It's pulled down from a top-tier score by a non-technical CEO, an AI capability that still seems nascent rather than proven, and a business model (consumer claims aggregation + law firm referrals) that is more services/ops-heavy than deep technology, which may limit engineering leverage relative to a pure product/infra company.
assessment.summary: Chariot Claims (chariotclaims.com), founded 2023 in Brooklyn/NYC by CEO Zim Hang, just raised a $10M Series A led by Silverton Partners (total funding $15.7M), confirming the exact headline in the prompt. The company helps consumers find and pursue legal claims over privacy violations, hidden fees, and hard-to-cancel subscriptions, working with ~20+ law firms and a small (~15-person) team, and is actively hiring multiple senior 'Engineering Lead' roles plus a technical product manager.
assessment.product: A consumer-facing platform that intakes user claims (surveys/questionnaires), screens eligibility via a mix of automation and human review, scans public records/court filings for case research, and is building AI tools to review supporting documents and determine claim validity; claims are then routed to a network of 20+ partner law firms for mass/class-action style pursuit.
assessment.team: CEO Zim Hang (3rd startup; prior background in healthcare tech, fintech, and web3; BS in Psychology & Neuroscience, Washington University in St. Louis). CTO Jon Chen (based in LA; prior engineering experience at Twitch, Rippling, and Coalition Inc.; Rutgers CS, incomplete). Other leadership: COO Sharon Cao, Product Strategy Lead Eric Tam, Head of Design Charlotte van den Bosch. Team size roughly 15 employees.
assessment.funding: Series A: $10M led by Silverton Partners (announced ~Oct 2026), with participation from Indicator Ventures, Lightbank, Neon Fund, ZVC, Rosecliff Ventures, Alumni Ventures, FJ Labs, Graph Ventures, and Vermilion Ventures. Prior: $3.6M seed in April/July 2025 led by Indicator Ventures, plus an earlier pre-seed. Total funding to date: $15.7M.
redFlags: CEO's background is not technical/engineering, and prior ventures include web3 experience, an area the candidate is explicitly skeptical of.
Business model depends partly on litigation/arbitration dynamics and a law firm referral network, which is less defensible as a pure technology moat.
AI component of the product is described as being developed, not yet a mature differentiator.
greenFlags: Currently hiring for four separate senior 'Engineering Lead' roles plus a Technical Product Manager, a strong signal that engineers are central to the company's roadmap, not an afterthought.
Small team (~15 people) post-Series A, meaning high potential leverage for an early engineering hire.
Real usage and revenue signals: 200,000+ monthly claim submissions, ~219,000 clients served historically, and the company describes itself as breaking even rather than purely burning seed cash.
CTO has solid engineering pedigree (Twitch, Rippling, Coalition Inc.).
Headquartered in New York City, matching the candidate's preferred geography.

name: Holo
evidence: Headline: Vilnius-based Holo raises €5M to bring AI-powered marketing to small businesses

Summary: AI marketing platform Holo has raised €5 million in a seed fundinground to further develop its marketing automation technology and reach moresmall businesses. The round was led by Market One Capital, ...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Holo (tryholo.ai) is a Vilnius, Lithuania-based AI marketing automation platform that lets small businesses auto-generate and publish ads, social posts, email campaigns and SEO content across channels like Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Vilnius, Lithuania, outside the US — materially harder to join given visa, relocation, or timezone gap for a US-based candidate; no explicit remote-hiring policy stated on their careers page.
Team already appears to be 30+ people across founders, engineering, design, support, marketing, ops, and content — not a tiny high-leverage team at this stage.

Founders (Deividas Kovger, Aleksandras Urbanavicius) have growth/paid-ads/email-marketing backgrounds rather than deep technical pedigree; CTO Arnas Puidokas's prior background wasn't surfaced in available sources.

Hiring mix includes a CMO, a 'Resident DJ,' and a YouTube content creator alongside one listed Senior Fullstack Engineer role — signals a generalist growth-stage scale-up more than an engineering-led org.
Marketing automation is a crowded, hype-adjacent category; not one of the person's named applied-AI verticals (legal/health/finance/logistics).
assessment.rationale: Holo has real, verified traction (reported $5M ARR in ~252 days, 4,000+ to 20,000+ paying customers depending on source, SOC2/ISO27001 compliance, live product with broad channel integrations) which argues against it being a thin GPT wrapper and fits the 'SaaS for SMBs' theme reasonably well. But it's headquartered outside the US with no stated remote policy, the team is already sizable rather than small/high-leverage, and the founders' backgrounds skew growth/marketing rather than deep technical — all of which cut against this person's stated priorities for joining as an engineer.
assessment.summary: Holo is a real, fast-growing AI marketing automation SaaS for small businesses, based in Vilnius and just closed a €5M seed led by Market One Capital. It has credible product traction, but its non-US location, already-sizable team, and marketing-growth-oriented founder backgrounds make it a middling fit for someone evaluating it as a place to join as an engineer.
assessment.product: An AI platform that analyzes a business's website/brand, then plans, generates, and auto-publishes marketing content (ads, social posts, email, SEO/blog) across 1,000+ integrated apps including Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok and Pinterest, aimed at small businesses without dedicated marketing teams.
assessment.team: Co-founders Deividas Kovger and Aleksandras Urbanavicius (growth strategy, paid ads, email marketing/martech backgrounds), with Karolis Vaiginis as design lead and Arnas Puidokas as CTO; team members previously worked with consumer brands including Sintra, Pulsetto, Burga and Moerie. Careers page shows ~30+ current team members across engineering, design, support, and marketing, based in Lithuania.
assessment.funding: €5M seed (reported as ~$5.6M in some coverage), led by Market One Capital, with participation from Silicon Gardens, FirstPick, Leonis Capital, NGL, Tekton Ventures, and business angels; previously raised under €1M.
redFlags: No remote-hiring policy stated despite being outside the US
Founding team's background is predominantly growth/marketing rather than deep engineering
greenFlags: Reported $5M ARR within 252 days with thousands of paying customers — real shipped product with traction, not just a seed-stage idea
Reputable seed investors (Market One Capital, FirstPick, Tekton Ventures)
Actively hiring a Senior Fullstack Engineer to 'own core architecture', a reasonably strong engineering signal
SOC2/ISO27001/GDPR compliance suggests real enterprise-grade engineering investment, not a superficial wrapper

The company plans to grow the team with this round.

name: Linkener
evidence: Headline: Barcelona-based Linkener raises €7.5 million to digitise and optimise energy management for businesses

Summary: Linkener, a Barcelona-based EnergyTech startup that digitises and optimises energy management for businesses through a platform combining consumption metering, data analytics and AI, has closed a €7.5 million funding round. The round was led by Klima Energy Transition Fund, Alantra’s energy transition fund, with GoHub Ventures remaining a shareholder. José Ignacio Ruiz, CEO of Linkener, […] The…
Headline: Linkener secures €7.5M to expand its energy management platform

assessment.whatTheyDo: Spanish EnergyTech company that sells business customers an energy management system built on proprietary remote metering, bill digitisation and AI analytics.
concerns: Based in Spain, not the US. Visa, relocation and time-zone gaps make it materially harder for a US-based person to join.
The EU press headline says Barcelona, but other sources point to Valencia. HQ is uncertain.
Mix of hardware metering, installation services (400+ solar/battery installs) and software. It looks closer to an energy services business than a pure software company.
Plans to grow partly through acquisitions, so engineers may spend time on integration work.
No careers page or open roles found, and no evidence of senior or staff engineering hiring.
Founder and team technical backgrounds are not verified. The CEO José Ignacio Ruiz has led since 2025, and the company appears to date from about 2011.
Energy efficiency for businesses is not one of the person's top themes.
assessment.rationale: The company is real and has traction (2,000+ customers, about 10,000 supply points). It has proprietary metering plus data and AI, and a credible €7.5M round from Alantra's Klima fund. But it is outside the US, in energy services rather than the person's core themes, and I found no evidence of engineering roles or founder technical depth. It is a plausible but weak fit for this person.
assessment.summary: Linkener is a Spanish EnergyTech company whose Intelligent Energy Management System (SIGE) meters consumption, digitises and validates bills, analyses supply contracts and recommends savings for businesses. It has 2,000+ customers and 400+ solar and storage installations. It raised €7.5M led by Alantra's Klima Energy Transition Fund, with existing shareholder GoHub Ventures staying in. It is a real, revenue-stage business, but Spain-based and services-heavy, which makes it a poor target for a US engineer looking for a high-leverage product role.
assessment.product: SIGE, an Intelligent Energy Management System built on proprietary remote metering. It tracks consumption, validates energy bills, analyses supply contracts, and sends alerts and savings recommendations. It also supports solar and battery projects. Customers are Spanish businesses.
assessment.team: CEO José Ignacio Ruiz, who has reportedly led the company since 2025. An unverified Dealroom profile credits Sergio Ferrer and Javier Severa as founders in 2011. Team size was not found.
assessment.funding: €7.5M round reported 19 October 2026, led by Klima Energy Transition Fund (Alantra). GoHub Ventures is an existing shareholder. Earlier rounds were not found.
techStack: Proprietary AI models for bill processing and anomaly detection
redFlags: Non-US company
Services and hardware-heavy business model
No visible engineering hiring
Conflicting HQ reports (Barcelona vs Valencia)
M&A-driven growth plan
greenFlags: 2,000+ customers and about 1.7 TWh of energy covered
Proprietary metering data and AI models, not a thin wrapper
Institutional lead investor with an energy-transition focus
Operating in a fragmented market

Combined with a non-US (Sweden) headquarters that raises relocation/visa friction, this lands in the weak-to-plausible band rather than a strong match.

assessment.team: Founder & CEO Per Österström, educated at Stockholm School of Economics, previously founded and scaled Sambla Group (consumer loan brokerage, 400+ employees, sold to Nordic Capital in 2021). No visible technical founder or engineering leadership disclosed.
Non-US headquarters adds relocation/visa friction for the target candidate.
greenFlags: Founder has prior successful exit (Sambla Group sold to Nordic Capital).
Experienced, credible chair with regulated consumer-finance background (ex-Nordnet CEO).

assessment.summary: OMass Therapeutics is an Oxford spin-out biotech that closed a Series C of about £230M (roughly $310M, reported as €275M by some outlets) in October 2026. assessment.team: Leadership includes Hsin Loke (COO) and Jon Roffey (SVP Discovery and Non-clinical); Ros Deegan was profiled by GV. I did not research founder backgrounds in depth.
assessment.funding: Series C of about £230M (roughly $310M; one outlet reports €275M) announced 15 Oct 2026, co-led by new investors Bain Capital Life Sciences, Forbion and Novo Holdings, with Janus Henderson Investors, SV Health Investors and Jefferson Life Sciences also participating. UK-based
Hiring is science-focused, not engineering
greenFlags: Clinical-stage lead asset in Phase 2
Strong, well-known investor syndicate
Differentiated mass spectrometry platform
